s: The lines “Desamunu preminchumanna, manchi annadi penchumanna” are associated with which poet and collection?
x: The lines were written by Gurajada Apparao and form part of Mutyala Saralu. The poem was published in Andhra Bharati.
tq: Use the poet–work pair directly; nearby nationalist poets are used as distractors.

s: Which one of the following statements correctly explains the idea expressed in the line “Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi”?
o: The nation is identified with its ruling dynasty.
The nation is represented only by its religious institutions.
The nation is defined by its geographical boundaries alone.
The nation consists primarily of its people rather than merely its soil.
x: Gurajada’s line means that a nation is its people, not merely its soil. It is part of the same poem in Mutyala Saralu.
tq: Translate the famous line into its precise underlying concept.

s: The poem containing “Desamunu preminchumanna” was called the national anthem of the Telugu people. In which periodical was it published?
x: Gurajada Apparao’s poem was published in Andhra Bharati and came to be regarded as the national anthem of the Telugu people.
tq: Separate the collection, periodical and title-related details of the same poem.

s: “Veera gandham tecchinaramu” is associated with which movement or period?
x: “Veera gandham tecchinaramu” was written by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy during the Salt Satyagraha era.
tq: Match the song with its historical occasion rather than merely its poet.

s: Who wrote the patriotic lyric “Ye desamegina ... pogadara nee talli bhoomi Bharatini”, commonly known by its title Janmabhoomi?
x: The patriotic lyric Janmabhoomi was written by Rayaprolu Subbarao.
tq: Identify the author from a distinctive line and title.

s: “Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu” was improvised on which occasion?
o: During the Salt Satyagraha at Dandi in 1930
During Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches at Rajahmundry in April 1907
During the Home Rule agitation in Madras in 1916
During Gandhi’s visit to Vijayawada in 1921
x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham improvised the song during Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches at Rajahmundry in April 1907.
tq: Lock the answer through the distinctive place, speaker and month-year combination.

s: “Ma Telugu Talliki mallepoodanda” later acquired which status?
o: It became the anthem of the Andhra University.
It became the official anthem of the Indian National Congress.
It became the national song of India.
It became the Andhra Pradesh State song.
x: The song written by Sankarambadi Sundarachari later became the Andhra Pradesh State song.
tq: Distinguish a state song from national and organisational anthems.

s: Who was known by the title “Abhinava Nannaya” according to the commission’s key and the accepted examination reference?
x: The accepted examination answer is Rayaprolu Subbarao. Although another source assigns the title to Viswanatha, the commission’s key and CDI assign it to Rayaprolu.
tq: Resolve a source-sensitive title by remembering the examination-key convention rather than the conflicting attribution.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Devulapalli Krishna Sastri was known as Andhra Shelley. Kavi Kokila is associated with Duvvuri Ramireddy, Telugu Lenka with Tummala Sitaramamurthy, and Kavi Samrat with Viswanatha Satyanarayana.
tq: Use elimination among closely related poet titles and avoid confusing popular epithets.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the titles associated with Gurram Jashuva is correct?
o: He was given Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti in 1946.
He was known as Andhra Shelley.
He received Viswakavi Samrat in 1936 from Vinukonda citizens.
He received Madhura Kavi Srinatha in 1964.
x: Gurram Jashuva was given the title Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti in 1946. He also had the titles Madhura Kavi Srinatha in 1952 and Viswakavi Samrat in 1964; Vinukonda citizens gave him Kavi Kokila in 1936.
tq: Discriminate among a poet’s multiple titles by checking the title-year association.

s: The title “Kavi Kokila” is associated with which poet, while it was also given to Gurram Jashuva by Vinukonda citizens in 1936?
x: Kavi Kokila is associated with Duvvuri Ramireddy. Vinukonda citizens also conferred the same title on Gurram Jashuva in 1936.
tq: Notice that one title can have both a conventional association and a separate conferral.

s: Who conferred the title “Madhurakavi” on Gurram Jashuva?
x: The title Madhurakavi was given to Gurram Jashuva by Viswanatha Satyanarayana.
tq: Identify the person who conferred a title, not merely the person who held it.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Poet)
a. Rayaprolu Subbarao
b. Gurajada Apparao
c. Viswanatha Satyanarayana
d. Unnava Lakshminarayana

List-II (Work)
i. Malapalli
ii. Andhravali
iii. Kanyasulkam
iv. Veyipadagalu

Select the correct code:
x: Rayaprolu wrote Andhravali, Gurajada wrote Kanyasulkam, Viswanatha wrote Veyipadagalu, and Unnava wrote Malapalli.
tq: Start from the sure pair and verify that every remaining work is used exactly once.

s: Which of the following works was written by Duvvuri Ramireddy?
x: Matru Desa Sankeertanam was written by Duvvuri Ramireddy. Swatantrya Rathamu is by Rayaprolu, Desabhakti Geyam by Gurajada, and Firdausi by Gurram Jashuva.
tq: Use direct author–work recall with works from neighbouring poets as distractors.

s: Kanyasulkam, first staged in 1893, was written by whom?
x: Kanyasulkam was written by Gurajada Apparao and was staged in 1893.
tq: Combine a work’s author with its distinctive staging year.

s:
Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Viswanatha Satyanarayana’s works?
1. Veyipadagalu received the Sahitya Akademi recognition.
2. Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu won the Jnanpith.
3. Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu was the first Jnanpith-winning work by a Telugu writer.
x: All three statements are correct. Veyipadagalu received Sahitya Akademi recognition, while Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu won the Jnanpith and was the first such award for a Telugu writer.
tq: Check the separate award associations before choosing the inclusive statement option.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Gabbilam was written by Gurram Jashuva, not Duvvuri Ramireddy. Duvvuri Ramireddy wrote Matru Desa Sankeertanam.
tq: Find the swapped author–work pair among otherwise familiar literary associations.

s: Who wrote Japaneeyamu, which celebrated Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905?
x: Japaneeyamu was written by Sriram Veerabrahmam of Bandar and celebrated Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905.
tq: Match the world event and patriotic work with the correct author.
sec: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author

s: Adipudi Somanatha Rao’s Japan Charitra was dedicated to whom?
x: Japan Charitra by Adipudi Somanatha Rao was dedicated to the Raja of Munagala. The Raja named his sons Togo and Nogi after Japanese commanders.
tq: Distinguish the dedicatee of a work from the historical figures who inspired it.
sec: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author

s:
Consider the following statements about Panchala Parabhavam:
1. It was written by Damaraju Pundarikakshudu.
2. It dealt with the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy.
3. Dyer was portrayed as Duryodhana.
4. Twenty-five students in Vizag were arrested for staging it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. The play concerned Jallianwala Bagh, cast Dyer as Duryodhana, was discussed in the British Parliament, and led to the arrest of 25 Vizag students who staged it.
tq: Treat the play, event, characterisation and consequence as separate factual components.
sec: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author

s: Which pair is correctly matched with the year of the patriotic play?
x: Padmavyuham was written by Kallakuri Narayana Rao in 1919. Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam was written by Umar Alisha in 1916.
tq: Check the author–title–year triad and reject swapped playwrights.
sec: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author

s:
Arrange the following works in chronological order of the years given:
A. Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam
B. Japan’s victory over Russia celebrated in Japaneeyamu
C. Padmavyuham
D. Kanyasulkam was staged
x: Kanyasulkam was staged in 1893, Japan’s victory occurred in 1905, Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam was written in 1916, and Padmavyuham in 1919.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the two middle events.
sec: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author

s: Which literary form did Rayaprolu Subba Rao pioneer in Telugu, drawing inspiration from Shelley and Keats?

s: What was the new poetic concept introduced by Rayaprolu Subba Rao?
x: Rayaprolu introduced Amalina Srungaram, a concept of platonic love.

s: Which of the following best describes Rayaprolu Subba Rao’s contribution to Telugu poetry?
o: He restored rigid prosody as the sole basis of Telugu poetry.
He replaced original verse with exclusively devotional compositions.
He moved away from translation of Sanskrit epics and introduced original, emotive verse.
He continued translating Sanskrit epics without alteration.
x: Rayaprolu broke with the translation of Sanskrit epics and brought original, emotive verse into Telugu. He also helped free Telugu poetry from rigid prosody.
tq: Choose the option that captures the complete literary change rather than an isolated label.

s: Who described Rayaprolu’s romanticism as “escapist”?
o: Progressive writers such as Sri Sri

Sri Sri’s call for progressive literature
Rayaprolu Subba Rao’s call for romantic poetry

s: Which statement about the circulation and reception of Garimella Satyanarayana’s nationalist song is correct?
o: It was cyclostyled a thousand times and praised by Gandhi.
It was published exclusively in a British government journal.
It was printed only once and was ignored by Gandhi.
It was circulated only among literary associations after independence.

s:
Consider the following statements about Garimella Satyanarayana:
1. His nationalist song was associated with the Non-Cooperation era.
2. He received a later sentence of two and a half years of rigorous imprisonment.
3. His wife, father and grandfather died while he was in jail.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The song belonged to the Non-Cooperation era, he later received two and a half years of rigorous imprisonment, and three close family members died during his imprisonment.
tq: Combine movement context, punishment and personal consequence without confusing the two imprisonment terms.

s: In which context did Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham improvise the patriotic verse beginning with “Bharata khandambu...” ?
o: During the 1907 speeches of Bipin Chandra Pal at Rajahmundry
During the Home Rule meetings led by Annie Besant
During the visit of the Simon Commission
x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham translated Bipin Chandra Pal’s 1907 speeches and improvised the verse at Rajahmundry.
tq: Link the poet, occasion, place and year in a single factual recall question.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the literary contribution of Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham at Rajahmundry?
o: He composed Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu and was jailed in 1922
He translated Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches and improvised a patriotic verse
He edited Golconda Patrika and wrote Gabbilam
He founded Bhavakavitvam and wrote Ekanta Seva

s: The later patriotic verse “Bharata khandambe okka pedda bandikhana” expressed India as which of the following?
o: A large prison under colonial rule
A prosperous kingdom protected by the British
A sacred land beyond foreign influence
x: The verse literally presents the Indian subcontinent as one large prison, conveying the reality of British colonial rule.
tq: Test the exact meaning of a quoted line rather than its author.

s: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham is recognised as the first Telugu national poet. Which work is associated with the distinction of being the first Telugu national song?
x: “Hinduvulara ennaallee gati” is recognised as the first Telugu national song, while Chilakamarti is recognised as the first Telugu national poet.
tq: Distinguish the poet’s title from the separately identified first national song.
sec: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham - patriotic verse, occasion, consequence

s: Which periodical was edited by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham?

tq: Apply the editor–periodical association and avoid confusing it with another Telugu publication.

s: Who is regarded as the founder of Bhavakavitvam?
x: Rayaprolu Subbarao is regarded as the founder of Bhavakavitvam.
tq: Use direct founder recall with closely related poets as distractors.

s:
Consider the following statements about Bhavakavitvam:
1. It emphasised romantic and personal emotion.
2. It included nature and love as important themes.
3. It sought freedom from classical prosody.
4. It had no patriotic strands.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Bhavakavitvam emphasised romantic and personal emotion, nature, love and freedom from classical prosody, and it also contained patriotic strands. Therefore, statement 4 is false.
tq: Find the one negating statement that reverses a feature of the movement.

s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of poets identified as major poets of Bhavakavitvam?
o: Basavaraju Apparao, Duvvuri Ramireddy, Devulapalli Krishna Sastri
Gurajada Apparao, Garimella Satyanarayana, Sri Sri
Bipin Chandra Pal, Rayaprolu Subbarao, Damaraju Pundarikakshudu
Kopparapu Subbarao, Krovvidi Lingaraju, Madduri Annapurnaiah
x: Basavaraju Apparao, Duvvuri Ramireddy and Devulapalli Krishna Sastri are listed among the main poets of Bhavakavitvam.
tq: Identify the complete group by separating movement poets from associated nationalist figures and prose contributors.

s: The Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu are associated with which work, described as the “Telugu Gitanjali”?
x: Ekanta Seva, associated with the Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu, is described as the “Telugu Gitanjali”.
tq: Match the literary group with its distinctive work and description.

s: Which of the following was the first Telugu play banned by the British?
x: Roshanara, authored by Kopparapu Subbarao, was the first Telugu play banned by the British.
tq: Use the superlative clue “first” and distinguish the action from later arrests and prosecutions.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the year and consequence associated with Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu?
o: 1931; its author was jailed for sedition under Section 124A
No year given; its performers were arrested in Vizag
x: Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu is associated with 1922, and its author Garimella was jailed.
tq: Separate closely related years and consequences in a proscribed-literature table.

s: Chicharapidugu was serialised during which period in Congress, and what consequence followed for its editor?
o: 1907–08; the work was banned as the first Telugu play
x: Chicharapidugu was serialised in Congress from 1927 to 1929, and its editor Madduri Annapurnaiah was jailed.
tq: Pair the publication period with the correct person and consequence.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Veerabali — Krovvidi Lingaraju — 1931 — jailed for sedition under Section 124A
Veerabali — Kopparapu Subbarao — first play banned by the British
x: Veerabali was written by Krovvidi Lingaraju in 1931, and he was jailed for sedition under Section 124A.
tq: Start with the sure author–work pair and verify the year and official consequence.

s: The work Tirugubatu was banned on the charge of:
x: Tirugubatu by Muni Manikyam Narasimha Rao was banned for “inciting the people”.
tq: Distinguish the stated ground for prohibition from the separate ground of sedition.

s: Who wrote Tirugubatu?
x: Tirugubatu was authored by Muni Manikyam Narasimha Rao.
tq: Apply the author–title association without confusing it with neighbouring proscribed works.

s: What was the immediate consequence associated with performances of Panchala Parabhavam?
o: The author was jailed for sedition under Section 124A
The work was banned for inciting the people
The editor of Congress was jailed
x: Performers of Panchala Parabhavam by Damaraju Pundarikakshudu were arrested in Vizag.
tq: Focus on the action taken against performers rather than the author or editor.

s:
Arrange the following works in chronological order according to the years specifically associated with them:
A. Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu
B. Chicharapidugu
C. Veerabali
D. Roshanara
x: Roshanara was the earliest item identified as the first banned play, followed by Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu in 1922, Chicharapidugu in 1927–29 and Veerabali in 1931.
tq: Fix the known first item, then arrange the dated works from 1922 through 1931.

s: Why did nationalist songs in spoken Telugu have a wider social reach than pamphlets?
o: They were written exclusively in classical prosody
They avoided political and social themes
They were restricted to educated urban readers
They could reach villagers who could not be reached effectively by pamphlets
x: Songs in spoken Telugu could reach villagers more effectively than pamphlets, thereby widening nationalist communication.
tq: Apply the communication advantage of spoken-language literature to a social situation.

s: Which literary development is associated with Gurajada in the growth of Telugu nationalist and progressive writing?
o: Banning all patriotic songs from public performance
Making vyavaharika bhasha a normal literary medium
Restoring exclusive dependence on classical prosody
Limiting Telugu literature to court poetry
x: Gurajada helped make vyavaharika bhasha, or spoken Telugu, a normal literary medium.
tq: Identify the specific linguistic contribution rather than a broad political claim.

s: The progressive writers later widened the social critique of Telugu literature primarily towards which issues?
x: Progressive writers extended the critique of society to caste and class issues.
tq: Select the paired social categories that define the later expansion of literary criticism.

s: At the World Telugu Mahasabhalu, which of the following set of Jnanpith awardees was recalled along with Gurajada and Sri Sri by Chief Minister Naidu?
o: Viswanatha, C. Narayana Reddy and Ravuri Bharadwaja
Rayaprolu Subbarao, Garimella Satyanarayana and Duvvuri Ramireddy
Kopparapu Subbarao, Krovvidi Lingaraju and Muni Manikyam Narasimha Rao
Basavaraju Apparao, Devulapalli Krishna Sastri and Madduri Annapurnaiah
x: Chief Minister Naidu recalled Gurajada, Sri Sri and the Jnanpith winners Viswanatha, C. Narayana Reddy and Ravuri Bharadwaja at the World Telugu Mahasabhalu.
tq: Test the complete membership of a named group rather than one isolated name.

s: The Bhava Kavitvam–Abhyudaya debate chiefly concerns whether romanticism was escapist or whether it:
o: Served as a necessary liberation of literary form
Eliminated all patriotic elements from poetry
Required a return to court literature
Made spoken Telugu unsuitable for public communication
x: The debate contrasts the criticism of romanticism as escapist with the view that it was a necessary liberation of literary form.
